results.per_judge: 6/12, 6/12, 12/12 (the Sonnet judge chose pvm-20-soft every time; the two Opus judges split evenly)
results.note: The lower bound clears 0.5 by 0.003, and the result depends on one judge. Before this change pvm-20 scored 22/36 against the same lottes images (not distinguishable). Read it as a small, fragile gain.
Judges who chose pvm-20 cited its clear scanlines and bloom; those who chose the soft preset cited pvm-20's dark gaps as artificial. pvm-20 stays the default, as the protocol fixed.

In every attempt (Opus three times over two slots, Sonnet once) frames 1 to 18 of the first clip came back as a request limit, so no full-view vote exists. Kept and hashed, not scored. The other clips of the same size loaded fully; the cause is unknown.

results.comparison: mix-bayer4 vs bayer4, game clip, PICO-8
results.note: Five of six reasons: mix keeps the green hills and hues; bayer4 turns them grey-blue. One preferred bayer4 as cleaner and finer.

pixel_template_mode.step2: mix-bayer4 flicker lower on both named sequences with PICO-8: pan 0.230 vs 0.245, game 0.115 vs 0.121 (evidence/shaders-dither-temporal-runs.json)
pixel_template_mode.caveat: Under a flickering light mix-bayer4 flickers about 2.8 times as much as bayer4; the rule did not weigh that because the template's light is steady. A template with flickering light should use bayer4.
pixel_template_mode.cost: SwiftShader, 480 x 270, 30 frames: mix-bayer4 773 ms per frame median against 62.5 ms for bayer4 (12 times slower; 16 plan steps over the palette per pixel). Not measured on the RTX 4090 (GPU reserved for training).

checks_on_the_judges: Part A: each judge chose the same image on all 14 swapped repeats and side A on exactly 14 of 28, so repeats may be copies. Part B: one agent per trial, so repeats come from different agents.
does_not_prove: Human preference; independence (all judges are Claude models and two share one model); anything beyond these frames and clips; the intervals treat repeats as independent.
